messages:
elena: Quick note — gateway -> async workers is still dropping important trace baggage when we republish (delayed retries / DLQs). I sketched a compact token approach to avoid embedding full OTLP blobs in SQS/Kafka attrs.
jon: yeah this has bitten us in prod. curious to see the token format.
elena: idea: encode (trace_id, parent_span_id, sampled_flag, small baggage kvs) into a single base64 token with a version and HMAC sig. store minimal data in the attr, keep canonical mapping in the worker when rehydrating. Advantages: fits attr size, deterministic parsing, sig prevents tampering.
kevin: :thinking: SQS msg attr limit is ~256KB but some queues are used with smaller limits and headers get lost on republish across brokers. Compact token makes sense. how small are we talking?
elena: target < 512 bytes typical. example (humanized):

```
RW-TOKEN v1 | tid=4f2a9d... | pid=1a2b3c | s=1 | b=u:12345,env:prod | sig=AbC...
```
encoded -> base64 and set as message attribute `rw-trace-token`.
raj: two things: 1) signing is necessary (or KMS-signed pointer) so downstream trusts it 2) avoid PII in baggage; we should blacklist keys and only allow whitelisted low-entropy ids.
jon: agree on whitelist. also need migration path: current services expect full OTLP headers (traceparent/baggage). worker rehydration should expand token -> inject `traceparent` for local spans and add links to original trace.
elena: exactly. worker pseudocode:
```
if attr.rw-trace-token:
  payload = decode_and_verify(attr)
  start_span(name, parent=payload.parent_span_id, links=[payload.trace_id])
  set_baggage(pick_whitelisted(payload.baggage))
else:
  start_new_trace()
```
kevin: what about retries / republished messages that accumulate stale tokens? we sometimes republish with modified payloads.
raj: canonicalize token when republishing: if worker republishes, it should recompute token with new parent_span set to current span id and include an "orig_tid" field to keep link back to first trace.
jon: storage/telemetry cost: note that if we blindly link every retry we'll blow up traces and retention. maybe sampling flag should be respected — if sampled=0 we only propagate ids but don't export spans.
elena: agreed. token contains `s` (0/1) and `policy` shorthand (e.g., `s=1;pol=erronly`) so exporters decide. Exporter config can drop low-value churn.
kevin: implementation notes: use AES-GCM + KMS for sig/encrypt? or HMAC with rotating keys. HMAC is simpler and avoids decryption but you can't hide field contents. we probably don't need encryption if we enforce no PII.
raj: prefer HMAC with per-region key rotation via KMS. Keep token compact by using binary packing (variant tags + varint) then base64.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy for `gateway-trace-token` feature started in us-west-2.
elena: next steps: 1) RFC doc w/ binary schema and whitelist keys 2) implement token lib in go/python SDKs 3) worker rehydrate shim and exporter gating by `s` + `pol`. I'll write RFC draft.
jon: +1. add tests for replayed tokens and DLQ republish behavior.
kevin: add a small perf test — encode/decode rate and attr size distribution. thx.
raj: also update security review for allowed baggage keys, and add a lint rule to block PII keys in token builder.
elena: I'll drop the RFC link here when ready. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
